title: The Hom-complex cone of an arbitrary sequential colimit is limiting
statement: Let C be a small category, J a Grothendieck topology, O a sheaf of commutative rings, F a sequential diagram of O-module cochain complexes, and N any O-module cochain complex. The cone with point Hom(colim F,N), and legs given by precomposition with colimit inclusions F_m -> colim F, is a limit of the diagram m -> Hom(F_m,N) over the opposite natural numbers. The Hom complex and its projections are those of [def-pur-hom-complex] and [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]. No boundedness, finite-freeness, Koszul hypothesis, or unit compatibility is involved.

source.place: Tag 0A0A, lemma-colim-and-lim-of-duals; Section 0A8X, section-hom-complexes; for finite evaluation also lemma-dual-perfect-complex and more-algebra.tex Tag 0913.

proof.text: Evaluate F at every source degree p. Evaluation preserves colimits of complexes. Package the existing sheaf tensor-Hom adjunction and its source naturality as a parametrized adjunction. Tensoring on the right preserves colimits by symmetry and closure. The parametrized-adjunction limit-preservation theorem therefore proves that internal sheaf Hom into N^(p+n), with its actual homObjMap precomposition maps, sends the evaluated colimit to a limit.

For a cone s over Hom(F_m,N) in degree n, project each leg to Hom(F_m^p,N^(p+n)). The componentwise precomposition formula makes these into cones over the limits from the first step. Lift each of them, and combine those lifts by the Hom-complex product universal property. Factorization and uniqueness follow after every product projection and every tower projection. Thus the canonical degree-n cone is limiting.

The cone legs are already chain maps by functoriality of Hom. Limits of complexes are created degreewise, so the degreewise limiting cones from the previous step prove that the original cone of complexes is limiting.

proof_origin.note: V4: the ordinary-complex refinement is proved by a private abstract product-cone argument, instantiated with the actual sheaf Hom functor and parametrized tensor-Hom adjunction.
